scenes.narration: The life of Yair Lapid begins far from where the story usually starts. He was prime minister of Israel from July to December 2022, the second alternate prime minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs under Prime Minister Naftali Bennett from 2021 to 2022, and Minister of Finance under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from 2013 to 2014. Before entering politics in 2012, Lapid was an author, TV presenter and news anchor.

Yair Lapid was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. Yesh Atid, which he founded, became the second-largest party in the Knesset by winning 19 seats in its first legislative election in 2013. From 2013 to 2014, following his coalition agreement with Likud, Lapid served as Minister of Finance under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

To understand where Yair Lapid ended up, start with where Yair Lapid began. He serves on the Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, and the Sub-Committee on Intelligence and the Security Services. On 17 May 2020, Lapid became the Leader of the Opposition, after the thirty-fifth government of Israel was sworn in.

The road from the beginning to the peak of Yair Lapid ran through years nobody filmed. On 5 May 2021, he began talks with other parties to try to form a coalition government. On 2 June 2021, Lapid informed Israeli President Reuven Rivlin that he had agreed to a rotation government with Naftali Bennett and was prepared to replace the incumbent prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Each stage of the life of Yair Lapid made the next stage possible. Lapid became the prime minister of Israel on 1 July 2022 after Bennett stepped down as prime minister following the dissolution of the Knesset. Lapid remained prime minister until a new government was formed after the November 2022 election.

The people who knew Yair Lapid young describe someone already restless. Serving for only 181 days, he is the shortest-serving non-interim Israeli prime minister. In April 2026, Yesh Atid formed a new political alliance with Bennett 2026 named Together.

What Yair Lapid built in the middle years is what the name still stands for. Yair Lapid was born in Tel Aviv, the son of journalist and politician Yosef "Tommy" Lapid, who served as Justice Minister, and novelist and playwright Shulamit (Giladi) Lapid. His father was born in Novi Sad, Yugoslavia (now Serbia) to Hungarian Jewish parents, and his mother was born in Tel Aviv.

By the time Yair Lapid reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. His maternal grandfather David Giladi, originally from Transylvania (now Romania), was a writer and journalist who was among the founders of the newspaper Maariv. His paternal grandfather Bela (Meir) Lampel, a lawyer and Zionist activist, was murdered in Mauthausen concentration camp, while his great-grandmother Hermione Lampel was sent to Auschwitz, where she was murdered in a gas chamber.

The rise of Yair Lapid was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. His childhood home in Tel Aviv was in the Yad Eliyahu neighborhood, in a residential building known as the Journalists' Residence, as several prominent journalists lived there. He attended high school at the Herzliya Hebrew Gymnasium, but struggled with learning disabilities and dropped out without earning a bagrut certificate.

Setbacks came early for Yair Lapid, and the response to them is the real story. Lapid spent most of his mandatory military service in the Israel Defense Forces as a military correspondent for the IDF's weekly newspaper, Bamahane ("In the base camp"). After completing his military service, he began working as a reporter for Maariv and published poetry in literary journals.

The legacy of Yair Lapid outlived the circumstances that produced it. The couple lives in the Ramat Aviv Gimel neighborhood of Tel Aviv. In 1988, at age 25, Lapid was appointed editor of Yedioth Tel Aviv, a local newspaper published by the Yedioth Ahronoth group.

Few lives travel as far as that of Yair Lapid, and the distance is the point. In 1991, he began writing a weekly column in a nationwide newspaper's weekend supplement—first for Maariv, and later for its competitor, Yedioth Ahronoth. In 1994, Lapid started on TV, hosting the leading Friday evening talk show on Israel TV's Channel 1.

The childhood of Yair Lapid contains the adult in small print. In 1997, he had an acting role in an Israeli film about the Gulf War, Song of the Siren. In the 1990s, Lapid hosted a current affairs talk show called "Yair Lapid" on Channel 2.

Money, luck and timing all played their parts in the life of Yair Lapid — in that order. From 1989 to 2010, Lapid wrote and published books spanning a variety of genres. His first was a thriller, of which he has published three more; the others include two children's books, two novels, and a collection of his newspaper columns.

The turning point in the life of Yair Lapid looked like a failure at the time. In addition, he wrote a drama series, War Room, that aired on Channel 2 in 2004. Lapid was also a songwriter for numerous Israeli musicians, among them Rami Kleinstein, Yardena Arazi, and Rita.

Every biography of Yair Lapid has to pass through the years that were quietly lost. Some of the songs he wrote became hits which reached the top of the charts in Israel. In January 2008, Lapid was the host of Ulpan Shishi (Friday Studio), Channel 2's Friday night news magazine.

The education of Yair Lapid happened mostly outside any school. That year, the Cameri Theater performed his first play, The Right Age for Love. In January 2012, controversy arose after Lapid was admitted by Bar-Ilan University into a doctorate program, studying towards a PhD in hermeneutics.

What Yair Lapid wanted at the start and what Yair Lapid got are not the same thing, and that gap is the story. This was in violation of rules stating that all doctoral candidates must hold at minimum a bachelor's degree. Lapid, who had failed to complete high school, was admitted to the university based on his extra-academic credentials and career in journalism and writing.

The defining trait of Yair Lapid was not talent — it was the refusal to stop. After the Knesset Education Committee launched an investigation, the Council for Higher Education canceled the program under which Lapid was admitted, which had allowed students without a BA to study towards a doctorate. On 30 April he formally registered his party, "Yesh Atid" (Hebrew: יש עתיד, lit., "There Is a Future").

Those who met Yair Lapid at the peak describe someone still running on the early hunger. The move was timed to coincide with the general expectation in Israel for early elections to be held in the early fall of 2012. A few days after Yesh Atid's registration, in a surprise move, Benjamin Netanyahu formed a national unity government.

The private years of Yair Lapid explain the public decades better than any speech. It was then thought that Lapid's party would have to wait until late 2013 before it could participate in national elections. But in October 2012, following the departure of Kadima from Netanyahu's coalition over how to implement a Supreme Court decision ending exemptions from Haredi conscription, Netanyahu announced that elections would take place in late January 2013, affording Yesh Atid its first opportunity to run.

The family Yair Lapid came from matters more than the legends admit. In November 2012, Yesh Atid was polling an average of 11.6%, or 13–14 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. The results of the January election showed the party winning an unexpected 19 seats, making Yesh Atid the second-largest party in the 19th Knesset.

The first real success of Yair Lapid arrived later than anyone expected, and changed everything. After the election, Yesh Atid joined the new government led by Netanyahu. At the same time, Netanyahu also dismissed Hatnua party leader Tzipi Livni from her cabinet post.

The last chapter of Yair Lapid was written long after the fame. Yesh Atid won eleven seats in the 2015 election, a decrease of eight seats. In the resulting Knesset, Yesh Atid sat in the opposition to a government headed by Netanyahu.

The whole life of Yair Lapid reads like a single decision repeated. Lapid and Yesh Atid claimed to spearhead the fight against corruption in Israel. The "Nachshon Plan", unveiled in 2017, stipulates that any person found guilty of corruption will be banned from serving in public office.

Between the birth and the legend of Yair Lapid lie the years that actually decide it. In the April 2019 and September 2019 elections, Yesh Atid joined the centrist Blue and White coalition headed by Benny Gantz. Yesh Atid again ran in the coalition for the 2020 election, but left the coalition after Gantz formed a unity government headed by Netaynahu (with plans for a rotation).

The reputation of Yair Lapid was built in the middle, not at the edges. On 5 May 2021, Lapid was entrusted with the second mandate to form a new government, after the incumbent Netanyahu failed to do so with the first mandate. On 9 May 2021, it was reported that Lapid and Bennett had made major headway in the coalition talks.

Somebody like Yair Lapid should not have made it — that is exactly why the story survives. However, on 10 May, coalition talks seemed to be jeopardized as the Ra’am party announced it was suspending coalition talks, due to escalation in the Israeli–Palestinian conflict. On 13 May his path to being Prime Minister was further complicated when Naftali Bennett reportedly decided against joining a Lapid government due to the ongoing military conflict with Gaza.

The life of Yair Lapid begins far from where the story usually starts. On 30 May 2021, Bennett announced in a televised address that Yamina would indeed join a unity government with Lapid, after all but one of Yamina's MKs agreed to back this decision. On 2 June 2021, following negotiations with Lapid and Bennett, Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas officially signed a coalition agreement with Lapid and agreed to allow his party to join.

Yair Lapid was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. The Knesset ultimately voted in favor of the new government by a one-vote margin on 13 June. the government was sworn in that same day, with Lapid becoming the Alternate Prime Minister of Israel and the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Upon becoming the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Lapid's ministry assumed the duties of the now-defunct Ministry of Strategic Affairs.

Several weeks later Lapid inaugurated Israel's embassy in Abu Dhabi, in what was the first official visit of the country by a member of the Israeli Government. In August 2021, he appointed former Minister of Health Yael German as Israeli Ambassador to France, and former Member of the Knesset Shimon Solomon as ambassador to Angola.

The road from the beginning to the peak of Yair Lapid ran through years nobody filmed. On 11 August, Lapid visited Rabat to inaugurate Israel's embassy in the city. In September, he inaugurated the Israeli Embassy in Manama, and announced the re-establishment of diplomatic relations with Sweden.

Each stage of the life of Yair Lapid made the next stage possible. Lapid became the caretaker Prime Minister of Israel on 1 July 2022, after the Knesset had voted to dissolve and call a snap election the previous day. The rotation government agreement had specified that if a snap election were called while Bennett was still prime minister, Lapid would rotate into the premiership and serve as caretaker prime minister until the next government would be formed after the election.
